title: A density version of the binary Goldbach problem, after Alsetri and Shao
abstract: A sorry-free Lean 4 proof, with no cited hypothesis, of Theorem 1.2 of A. Alsetri and X. Shao, Density versions of the binary Goldbach problem, arXiv 2405.18576v2, Acta Arith. 218, 2025, 285 to 295: if A is a set of primes whose relative lower density in every reduced residue class b mod W is at least some eta > 1/2, then almost all even positive integers are a sum of two primes from A. The entry also proves the paper's Theorem 1.1, that relative density 1 - epsilon in the primes alone does not suffice, and the sharpness of the constant 1/2 stated in its Remark 1.3. A derived result of this entry, not a result of the paper, shows that the hypothesis of Theorem 1.2 holds for the set of all primes, so the theorem is not vacuous. Binary Goldbach is open and is not claimed; Theorem 1.2 concerns almost all even numbers. An AI agent wrote the Lean code, except the ported PrimeNumberTheoremAnd code credited to its authors; the statements were checked against the paper by an AI agent and are offered for human audit.
